title: ‘Not designed for confidence’: the new configurations of confinement
abstract: In recent years, ‘modernization’ has been used by successive governments as a justification for expanding and legitimating prison expansion. Drawing on prisoner and staff experiences of different architectural layouts of prison accommodation, this article considers the implications of the wave of ‘modernization’ that saw tiered and galleried landings replaced by separate-floored housing units. We use empirical data to discuss the consequences of this change for security, meaningful interactions, effective staff development and prisoner mobility. As the galleried landing quietly vanishes from the contemporary carceral landscape, we outline implications for staff recruitment, development and retention. Our data show that the lived experience of galleried prisons reveals a disparity between their assumed obsolescence and their continued relevance in shaping contemporary carceral experiences.
